title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot for administrators in GCC
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a preview API for blocking catalog agents, so the blanket statement that blocking has no API needs correction. The indirect-cost-only rating also conflicts with the roadmap's requirement for a tenant to hold a Copilot add-on licence. The roadmap facts and both cited admin paths are supported; GCC-specific implementation details remain unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Agents > Registry > Microsoft 365 Admin > Block reaches the Admin agent's blocking action; its documentation also permits scoped deployment.
claims.quote: Select to Agents > Registry. ... Locate Microsoft 365 Admin in the registry. ... Use the available agent actions to Block the agent or to scope deployment to specific users or groups instead of the entire organization.
claims.fix: Keep the feature-specific path, but add this note: 'The general agent-actions documentation instead gives Agents > All agents > agent > Block.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions in sources.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API call for the standard agent blocking control used by the Microsoft 365 Admin agent.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: Replace the blanket API absence with the documented general catalog-agent control: graph call 'POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-block. Note: 'Preview; requires Microsoft Agent 365 and delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All. Blocks the selected catalog package; GCC availability of this API is not confirmed.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview, which states that a package represents an agent or tool in the organization catalog. Replace the prose absence with 'The catalog package blocking API is documented in preview; no API for the Microsoft Copilot in admin centers access setting was found.'
